title.narrative: FOND. HIRONDELLE 2018-2023 Studio Tamani: Info for dialogue, peace and equality
FOND. HIRONDELLE 2018-2023 Studio Tamani: Info för dialog, fred, jämlikhet

description.narrative:
Fondation Hirondelle, a non-profit organization based in Switzerland working to strengthen independent media in especially conflict-affected countries, has submitted an application to Sida for support to the project Studio Tamani - news and information for dialogue, peace and equality in Mali, for the period 2018-2022. Sida has previously contributed to Studio Tamami during the period 2015-2017. Studio Tamani is a media platform for professional and impartial news and information. Through a network of 70 local partner radios, covering 85% of Mali's population, daily news and debate programs are broadcasted in five languages. In addition, thematic programmes on children's and women's rights, shortly also on environmental and climate issues, are broadcasted every week. Moreover, social media are increasingly being used to reach especially the younger part of the population.
The overall objective of the intervention is to contribute to peace and development in Mali through information and dialogue between all peoples and all regions of the country and the two specific objectives are that the Malian population is better informed and more engaged in supporting the peace process, democracy, gender equality and a fairer society thanks to its access to independent, professional information and debate programs, and that Studio Tamani becomes a sustainable project run by a Malian legal entity and fully gender mainstreamed.
The total budget of the intervention is 87.2 MSEK, of which Sweden contributes with 51.6 MSEK. In addition to this amount, Sida provides 500 000 SEK to be disposed by Sida to support strengthening of Fondation Hirondelle's capacity for results based management. The other main donors are currently the EU and Denmark.

Fondation Hirondelle, en ideell organisation baserad i Schweiz som arbetar med att stärka oberoende media i framförallt konfliktdrabbade länder, har till Sida inkommit med en ansökan om stöd till projektet Studio Tamani - nyheter och information för dialog, fred och jämlikhet i Mali, under perioden 2018-2022. Sida har tidigare bidragit med stöd till Studio Tamani under perioden 2015-2017. Studio Tamani är en mediaplattform för produktion av professionella och opartiska nyheter och information. Genom ett nätverk av 70 lokala partnerradiostationer som täcker 85% av Malis befolkning sänds dagliga nyhets- och debattprogram på fem olika språk. Varje vecka sänds dessutom tematiska program om barns- och kvinnors rättigheter och inom kort även om miljö- och klimatfrågor. Sociala medier används också i allt högre utsträckning för att nå särskilt den yngre delen av befolkningen.
Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att bidra till fred och utveckling i Mali genom information och dialog mellan alla människor och regioner i landet. Det två specifika målen är att befolkningen är bättre informerad och mer engagerad i att stödja fredsprocessen, demokrati, jämställdhet och ett rättvisare samhälle tack vare tillgången till oberoende och professionella informations- och debattprogram, samt att Studio Tamani uppnår hållbarhet, drivs av en malisk juridisk person och är fullt jämställdhetsintegrerad.
Insatsens totala budget är 87,2 MSEK varav Sida bidrar med 51,6 MSEK. Utöver detta belopp tillhandahåller Sida 500 000 SEK som ska disponeras av Sida för att bidra till att stärka avtalsparten Fondation Hirondelles kapacitet för resultatbaserad styrning. De andra huvudsakliga givarna är i dagsläget EU och Danmark.

The overall objective of the intervention is to contribute to peace and development in Mali through information and dialogue between all peoples and all regions of the country. The two main expected results are that the Malian population is better informed and more engaged in supporting the peace process, democracy, gender-equality and the development of a fairer society thanks to its access to independent, professional information and debate programmes and that Studio Tamani at the end of the project period has become a sustainable project that is fully gender mainstreamed and run by a Malian entity.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
Based on final reporting and other communication, results achieved over the project period can be summarised as follows:
- The broadcasting network of partners was extended from 70 in 2018 to 85 at the end of 2022 and three (03) television channels (Renouveau TV, Africable TV and Mandé TV). It has increased the program distribution across the country and made it accessible to a large majority of the Malian population. Since the end of 2022, 88% of the country's population has the opportunity to receive Studio Tamani programs. In addition, the audience study carried out in March 2023 by the Immar Institute shows that 3.4 million of the Malian population aged 15 and over, listen to Studio Tamani's programmes every week, i.e. more listeners than in 2017.
Furthemore, the percentage of the Malian population that has access to Studio Tamani (ST) programs has risen from 75% to 85% (data from the last audience survey in 2023). Therefore, the objective of 85% for geographical coverage of ST programs has been achieved. Broadcasting in five (5) local languages (French, Bambara, Peuhl, Tamasheq and Sonrhaï) has contributed to the understanding of information and awareness raising messages through communication and has encouraged dialog and cohesion.
- Studio Tamani has responded throughout the five years to strong and sometimes vital information needs of the Malian population, through its daily treatment of topics directly related to crisis factors in the country. Its role as a forum and media platform essential to restore the channels of dialogue and peace has been strengthened through its talk-show "Le Grand Dialogue", broadcast daily by partner radios and in video version by a cable TV in Bamako. This program, recognized and appreciated in particular by the peace process actors, has given the floor to all Malian society components, including groups in conflict, on a daily basis.
- The 3.15 hours daily program produced by Studio Tamani and broadcast by its partner radios network (1h on weekends and public holidays) is now well known, recognized and appreciated in all regions of the country especially those facing the most violent consequences of the crisis. Compared with recent audience surveys carried out by Immar Institute in 2023, Studio Tamani's total radio audience (from adults) remains stable in terms of coverage (31% in 2023 vs 32% in 2017). The weekly audience is increasing in quantitative terms (300,000 listeners on average per week). There is also a higher proportion of listeners who consider Studio Tamani programs to be indispensable, whatever the geographical area. The adult's audience survey from 2023 shows that many (86%) of listeners have very high level of confidence in ST's broadcasts.
- The gender approach was a key priority for the project. As part of its challenge on gender equality, ST has dedicated important efforts to improve the gender content. A "Women" database has been created by the editorial staff to make it easier for journalists to find female correspondents and thus encourage more women to speak out. ST has continued production of a multimedia programme to promote women's rights and gender equality in Malian society. For instance, in 2022, 24.21% of the speakers in all Studio Tamani programs were women with an increase of 4.21% compared to the year 2021. With the special edition "All the women of Mali", Malian women benefit from more content and/or topics related to the promotion and defense of their fundamental rights.
- The project's sustainability strategy focused on skills transfer to the Malian management team. In this regard, various capacity building sessions have been carried out for ST's staff, partner radio stations and correspondents in the various regions. All over the project, more than 350 participants (journalists, correspondents, trainees, students) took part in various workshops. ST's management team is more professional and has taken editorial responsibility for all the studio programs.
In sum, the project "Studio Tamani, reference and sustainable information for dialogue, equality and peace in Mali" has contributed to the achievement of the objectives of the government and its technical and financial partners. Conceived in a time of crisis, the project has responded to the concerns of national authorities and the population who are facing the resurgence of disinformation and stigmatization messages. The various activities carried out during the 2018-2022 period contributed to the achievement of results, especially in terms of access to quality, neutral and impartial information.
It has been a relevant tool adapted to the needs of media personnel. Its added value lies in the improvement of media governance in Mali and the availability of a pool of qualified resources and skills, constituting the foundation of sustainability.
As an independent, neutral and impartial media, ST in collaboration with the various partners has contributed to improving the level of knowledge of the population on current issues (GBV, climate change, conflicts, education, health, elections, etc.) and promoted awareness of the gender disparity within society as a whole. The continuous increase in the geographical coverage rate (85%), the implementation of the free number, the use of several communication channels (Facebook, Twitter, Youtube, etc.), the facilitation of debates, the installation of listeners' clubs, etc., are all elements that have facilitated the achievement of results and induced changes in behaviour at the individual, family and community levels.
However, despite the effects induced by the project, the sustainability of ST is a niche where we must continue with the reflections. With the current context, the withdrawal of donors is likely to hurt ST's operations because the level of funds raised by ST does not cover the financial needs of the organization as well as those of partner radio stations.
Furthemore, to raise the level of women's participation in "Grand Dialogue" is another aspect to be followed-up. Despite the efforts put in place by the Studio Tamani team, women are still reluctant to participate in the live debate "Grand Dialogue". In fact, the target 20% mentioned in the logical framework has not been reached.
From 2019 to 2022, the information relayed concerned all the regions of Mali. In the last year of implementation, the regions of Sikasso and Kayes were much more covered.
With regard to the programmatic balance between the categories of stakeholders in the radio program "Grand Dialogue", the number of participants from civil society increased from 20% in 2018 to 33.58% in 2022. There has been also a slight increase in the number of women taking part in the "Grand Dialogue" from 11.13% in 2021 to 15.71% in 2022.
However, the target 20% mentioned in the logical framework has not been reached.
Women's rights receive special attention in Studio Tamani's productions
From 2020 onwards, the number of women taking part in the "Gran Dialogue" has fallen down from 28.3% to 7.02% in 2022. Women find difficult to take part in live debates. Fear linked to the period of transition is a determining factor in the low participation of women in the "Grand Dialogue".
According to the 2022 annual report, various awareness-raising campaigns have been carried out to raise the level of women's participation in "Grand Dialogue". Despite this, women became reluctant to take part in the debates. However, they are comfortable with magazines.
Social issues are on the political agenda
Regarding the participation of power players that intervene on ST, it can be seen that from 2021 onwards, the turnout rate began to fall. Fear of freedom of expression could be cited as the main cause of this fall.
In terms of the percentage of ST's programs addressing governance issues, newspapers are dealing more with governance issues than magazines.
Regarding the percentage of ST's programs addressing environmental issues, it has been found that magazines cover environmental issues the most.
Regarding the contribution to the sustainability of ST, the follwing results have been achieved:
Department heads are gradually assuming more direct responsibility for managing ST
To ensure sustainability, ST has been involved in the vocational training of trainees from various training institutions and partner radio stations. A total of 24 trainees in professional immersion, including 14 women, benefited from the project's capacity building.
To provide practical solutions to the concerns of partner radio stations, ST has carried out follow-up training missions in collaboration with head office (Fondation Hirondelle). The number of women receiving training was higher than that of men, at 63.6% compared with 36.4% for a total of 55 participants.
Studio Tamani strengthens its capacity to produce awareness campaigns to boost revenues
Internal funding is mobilized through income-generating activities. Financial resources have been generated through campaigns on several themes (public accountability and women's participation; civic engagement; migration; civil status; coronavirus and health; corruption and social protection) with NGOs and civil society as the main sponsors. To achieve this, a partnership was established with various organizations such as FHI350, Mali Justice Project, OIM,Cowater International, etc.
ST is gender-sensitive at institutional and programme level
Various gender initiatives have been carried out. The gender action plan has been partially implemented. Studio Tamani currently has 35% of female editorial staff and expanded its network of regional correspondents in early 2019 with the addition of 8 women. This quota of 35% of women slightly exceeds what is provided for by the Law No. 2015-052/ of 18 December 2015 instituting measures to promote gender in access to nominative and elective functions. ST has established a database of women with skills to discuss and make women's voices heard for better protection of their fundamental rights.
The Board of Tamani Association is operating in accordance with its articles of association at the end of 2022
The creation of the Studio Tamani Association in 2017 was intended to perpetuate ST after the partners withdrew. With this in mind, Fondation Hirondelle and Association Tamani signed a partnership agreement at the end of 2018. According to the 2019 annual report, the strategies for operationalizing sustainability consisted of building the capacity of the board of directors and recruiting a sustainable coordinator.
The occurrence of Covid-19 and the consecutive departure of three Fondation Hirondelle representatives between 2021 and 2022, including two in the space of 6 months in 2021, had an impact on the Tamani Association Board of Directors.The level of achievement of this objective has not lived up to expectations. Irregularities in the running of meetings have meant that practical measures have not been adopted. On the other hand, a number of achievements have been made, including improving the level of knowledge and skills of staff at central and operational levels, and developing a project management culture. The current representative, who took up his post in 2022 for one year, has not been able to remedy the weaknesses reported.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
